CPESR Exam 1 — Tagging Pilot

First 8 of 55 questions, transcribed + tagged from the image-based source. Format matches fs_simulator.html's schema (cat/topic/program).

Q1. Which among the following is/are true regarding LiDAR? 1. LiDAR is a surveying method that measures distance of a target by illuminating that target with a pulsed laser light, and measuring the reflected pulses with a sensor. 2. It is the most accurate data transmission technique in which light is used as medium.
IIlidar
  • A) 1 only
  • B) Neither 1 nor 2
  • C) 2 only
  • D) Both 1 and 2
LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) is a remote sensing method using pulsed laser light to measure distance to a target. Statement 2 is false — LiDAR is not a "data transmission technique."

Answer: A
Q2. A sewer lateral is to be installed at sta 21+37.45 on center. The connection to the sewer main (sewer wye) is 18 in in length. There is a break of the sewer line at sta 21+38.49. The break has to be cleared by a minimum of 6 in. The sewer main line must be inserted 3 in into the wye or any connecting pipe to secure it on both sides. What is the minimum distance that needs to be cut out of the sewer mainline to install the sewer wye and lateral?
Vconstr

  • A) 1.54 ft
  • B) 1.29 ft
  • C) 1 ft
  • D) 1.71 ft
First cut: 2138.49+0.5: First cut: 2138.49+0.5=2138.99 Second cut constrained at south end: 2137.45−5/12+3/12: second cut constrained at south end: 2137.45−\(\dfrac{5}{12}\)+\(\dfrac{3}{12}\)=2137.28 2138.99−2137.28: 2138.99−2137.28=1.71 ft.

Answer: D
Q3. The field notes for a road centerline are shown (BM1 elev 111.73 through BM2 elev 110.67, with BS/FS readings and a 6+00 cross-section note). What is the slope from the centerline at Sta 4+00 to Sta 6+00, 60 ft right of centerline?
IIIlevel

  • A) 0.66%
  • B) −1.14%
  • C) 1.19%
  • D) −1.19%
Elev at 4+00: Elev at 4+00 = 111.73+4.30−4.48 = 111.55 Elev at 60 ft right of 6+00: elev at 60 ft right of 6+00 = 109.17 (chaining the FS/BS through the notes) Horizontal length: horizontal length = √(200²+60²) = 208.806 Slope: slope =\(\dfrac{(109.17-111.55)}{208.806}\)= −1.14%.

Answer: B
Q4. A new highway alignment requires a horizontal curve. Point A (N20324.77, E13965.48) is on the alignment before the curve; Point C (N20108.44, E19700.25) is after the curve; Point B (N22146.51, E16400.48) is the PI. What is the central angle of this curve?
IIItrav
  • A) 53°11'53"
  • B) 68°30'11"
  • C) 58°17'56"
  • D) 111°29'49"
Bearing AB: Bearing AB = N53.19808°E (from lat/dep of A→B) Bearing BC: bearing BC = S58.29886°E (from lat/dep of B→C) Central angle: central angle = 180−53.19808−58.29886 = 68.5031° = 68°30'11".

Answer: B
Q5. The survey crew is being asked to extend a level circuit across a canyon 1150 ft wide, with equipment access only from either side of the cliffs. Which technique should be used?
IIlevel
  • A) Spherical leveling
  • B) Cross sectional leveling
  • C) Reciprocal leveling
  • D) Concentrical leveling
Reciprocal leveling extends a circuit across a wide barrier by taking backsights from turning points on each side and averaging the two HI determinations to cancel curvature/refraction.

Answer: C
Q6. A measurement was obtained using a steel tape found to be shorter than its actual length when the temperature was above standardized temperature. The temperature was consistent throughout the survey. What type of error is this?
IIItheory
  • A) Random error
  • B) Natural error
  • C) Cumulative error
  • D) Accidental error
A consistent temperature means the same error was applied to every measurement — a cumulative (systematic) error.

Answer: C
Q7. A surveying plane's flight height is 4,000 ft above sea level, camera focal length 8.25 in. What is the photo scale at Point 1 (elev 900 ft) and Point 3 (elev 125 ft)?
IVphoto

  • A) 1:566 / 1:479
  • B) 1:376 / 1:470
  • C) 1:576 / 1:870
  • D) 1:286 / 1:323
Scale: Scale = f/(H−h): Point 1 =\(\dfrac{8.25}{(4000-900)}\)= 1 in=375.76 ft Point 3: Point 3 =\(\dfrac{8.25}{(4000-125)}\)= 1 in=469.69 ft.

Answer: B

VhcProgram S — partial

Q11. A redesigned highway has shoulder-to-shoulder width 44 ft; a curve must clear a light pole by 9 ft on the outside edge (pole is 17 ft off centerline, I=24°53'40"). What is the centerline radius?

Q12. BVC sta 5+00 elev 250.00, +5.5% grade in; EVC sta 29+00 elev 358.00, +3.5% grade out. Typical cross section: 22 ft to edge at 2%, then 10 ft at 2% down to toe, 6" curb. What is the elevation of the toe of slope at sta 19+50?

Q13. A grid survey plot with spot elevations at each grid node is shown (100'×100' cells, contour interval 10). Which of the four contour drawings (A–D) correctly represents the elevations?

Q15. Stadia setup: K=100.50, C=0. Backsight to A: stadia interval 7.2−6.9 (angle 6°31'40" is extraneous — sight is level). Foresight to C: stadia interval 4.7−3.3, vertical angle 39°. What is the horizontal distance A to C?

Q16. Lot corners: A (N3476.56, E1535.82), B (N−1617.16, E2127.39), C (N−2564.83, E−2131.91). What is the area of the parcel?
IIItravProgram A — partial

Shoelace formula: Area: Shoelace formula: Area = ½|X_A(Y_B−Y_C)+X_B(Y_C−Y_A)+X_C(Y_A−Y_B)| = 11,128,147.37 ft² = 255 acres. Q17. Triangle Building/Store/2+25 baseline: Δ1=63°40', Δ2=20°18', baseline segment (3+00 to 2+25) = 75 ft, (3+95 to 3+00) = 95 ft. What is the length from the SE corner of Building to NE corner of Store?

Q18. An easement area needs recording. Line AB is 300 ft with a slope of 1/1.5 with respect to bearings N88°E/S2°E; what is the area of the 40-ft wide easement?
IIIarea

  • A) 0.245 ac
  • B) 0.265 ac
  • C) 0.235 ac
  • D) 0.255 ac
∠A: ∠A = 90−tan⁻¹(\(\dfrac{1}{1.5}\)) = 56.31° X₁: x₁=\(\dfrac{40}{tan56.31}\)=26.67 ∠B: ∠B=180−90−56.31=33.69° X₂: x₂=\(\dfrac{40}{tan33.69}\)=60 CD: CD=300−26.67−60=213.33 Trapezoid area: trapezoid area = (\(\dfrac{40}{43560}\))[\(\dfrac{(300+213.33)}{2}\)] = 0.235 ac.

Answer: C
Q19. Distance measurements are to be taken in the Sierra National Forest. Which instrument would be used in a wooded area?
IIfield
  • A) Theodolite
  • B) EDM
  • C) Level
  • D) GPS
Tree canopy blocks GPS satellite connection theodolites/levels don't measure distance directly. An EDM is the only workable choice, though EDMs are typically inaccurate under 200 ft.

Answer: B
Q20. A high voltage power line will be extended through the foothills into the adjacent city. What type of survey is best used for this extension?
Iintro
  • A) Utility survey
  • B) Aerial survey
  • C) Route survey
  • D) Construction survey
For long stretches of linear works, a route survey is best utility survey only shows what exists, aerial isn't suited for long linear projects, construction survey is for build measurements.

Answer: C
Q21. On the contour map shown (interval 10, innermost closed contour at B labeled 90), what is the elevation of Point B?
IVtopo

  • A) 98
  • B) 92.5
  • C) 94
  • D) 100
B sits inside the 90 contour with no higher contour shown, so its elevation is anything between 90 and the next interval (100), but not exactly on a contour line — 98 is the best answer among the choices.

Answer: A

  • A) 1:3000
  • B) 1:1320

Scale: Scale =\(\dfrac{f}{(H-h)}\)=\(\dfrac{6 in}{(9400-1500)}\)=\(\dfrac{6 in}{7900 ft}\)= 1:15,800.

Q23. The favored method of obtaining the most accurate coordinates of Point R, approximately 1600 ft from Point Q, is
IIfield
  • A) Total Station
  • B) Transit

A total station gives the most accurate coordinates at this range GPS is second-best.

Answer: A
Q24. The town wants to know if a new hotel is being built in an area marked on the FEMA Flood Map. Which survey does the city engineer need for the assessment?
Iintro
  • A) Topographic Survey
  • B) Control Survey
  • C) Hydrographic Survey
  • D) Route survey
A topographic survey is used to assess flood-zone/elevation questions like this.

Q25. A circular borrow area has boundary elevation 1715' throughout; square-yard cross-section areas are given at +5/+10/+15/+20 ft above that boundary (65.5, 178.2, 93, 140 SY respectively). How much cut is there below elevation 1730 to level the borrow pit?
IIIarea

  • A) 210 yd³
  • B) 1870 yd³
  • C) 210 yd³
  • D) 1170 yd³
1730−1715: 1730−1715=15 ft, so the +5/+10/+15 layers count (the +20 layer is above 1730 and excluded): 5(65.5×9)+10(178.2×9)+15(93×9)+15(140×9) = 50,440.5 ft³ ÷ 27 = 1868.17 yd³ ≈ 1870 yd³.

Answer: B
Q26. Which of the following can be used to determine a watershed area?
IVtopo
  • A) Flood map
  • B) Hydrological map
  • C) Parcel map
  • D) Topographic map
Watershed determination needs elevations/contours — a topographic map. Hydrological maps show water bodies, flood maps show flood risk, parcel maps are irrelevant here.

Q32. Differential leveling field notes (BM R through BM S) have several blanks. The missing data for point C (a side-shot monument, FS=7.04, under the HI=125.69 set at TP2) is
IIlevel

  • A) 123.82 ft
  • B) 118.42 ft
  • C) 118.65 ft
  • D) 125.46 ft
HI stays constant at 125.69 through all side shots off TP2 until the next turning point Elevation of C: elevation of C = HI − FS = 125.69 − 7.04 = 118.65 ft.

Q33. Which of the following applications can GIS be used for?
IVgis
  • A) Quantity takeoffs
  • B) Utility map
  • C) Mass diagram
  • D) Grading plans
GIS suits general-purpose queries like locating utility lines in an area grading plans, mass diagrams, and quantity takeoffs all need detailed elevation data too fine-grained for typical GIS use.

Answer: B
Q34. Two right triangles share vertical side X; left triangle has base 349.93' and base angle 33°0'0", right triangle (area 69,408 ft²) has base angle 39°0'0". What is distance X?
IIItheoryProgram T — partial

  • A) 414.04'
  • B) 142.14'
  • C) 124.82'
  • D) 136.79'
X: X = tan(33°)(349.93+b) where b is the right triangle's base, and also X=tan(39°)·b with ½·b·X=69,408 — solving simultaneously (quickest: b=538.85 total baseline via area/tan relationship, X=538.85−414.03=124.82'). Program T's right-triangle branches can solve each triangle individually once one side is known, but chaining the shared unknown X across both triangles is manual.

Answer: C
Q35. Point X (N550, E450), Point Y (N600, E875). Bearing of XZ = N28°47'E, bearing of YZ = N61°58'W. What are the coordinates of Point Z?
IIItravProgram H — full

  • A) N763.77, E567.42
  • B) N734.13, E536.81
  • C) N744.42, E547.24
  • D) N754.33, E556.85
Classic two-known-point, two-bearing intersection — exactly what Program H solves. Convert each bearing to the interior angle measured off baseline XY at each known point, then XEQ H ENTER with X's coordinates, Y's coordinates, and the two angles (remembering the program's X=Easting/Y=Northing convention, reversed from standard N/E). Z = N763.77, E567.42.

Answer: A

Q37. Plane surveying is defined as
Itheory
  • A) surveying when less accurate surveying equipment is used

Plane surveying treats the earth's surface as flat, neglecting curvature.

Q38. A rectangular park is proposed: 740±0.14 ft by 290±0.06 ft. What is the area of the park?
IIItheory
  • A) 214,600±0.20 ft²
  • B) 214,600±60.16 ft²
  • C) 214,600±85 ft²
  • D) 214,600±170 ft²
Error propagation: Error: Error propagation: Error = √[(740²)(0.06²)+(290²)(0.14²)] = ±60.16 ft² Area: Area = 740×290 = 214,600±60.16 ft².

Q39. A building pad has finished grade at 96 ft: 12 in concrete on 6 in aggregate base. Site plan: 150'×100' pad, corner elevations 98.5/98.5/96.0/96.0. What is the total excavation?
Varea
  • A) 1530 CY
  • B) 830 CY
  • C) 1560 CY
  • D) 2220 CY
Volume above FG (avg-end-area): 150×100×(98.5−96)/2: Volume above FG (avg-end-area) = \(\dfrac{150\times 100\times (98.5-96)}{2}\) = 18,750 ft³ Volume for base+concrete below 96: (18/12)×100×150: volume for base+concrete below 96: (\(\dfrac{18}{12}\))×100×150 = 22,500 ft³ Total: total = 41,250 ft³ ÷ 27 = 1528 CY ≈ 1530 CY.

Answer: A
Q40. A mountain road in the Angeles Forest has 245 ft of proposed roadway length on this stretch (sheet 2). Given the contour map and the road cross-section (40% slope face, CP-to-HP at 0.75:1), what is the excavated volume for this stretch?
Varea

  • A) 73,000 CY
  • B) 22,000 CY
  • C) 37,000 CY
  • D) 51,000 CY
Key insight: the road cross-section shown is a side view along the roadway (the road can't run directly into that steep a slope face-on), so the 245 ft given length is the distance along the roadway — not the cross-section width — and the cross-sectional cut area is multiplied by that 245 ft length to get volume.

Answer: D
Q41. A curve is staked from Point T (sta 12+45) to Point U. The straight (chord) distance T to U is 570 ft, central angle 35°. What is the approximate station at Point U?
VhcProgram S — full
  • A) 18+15
  • B) 5+79
  • C) 18+24
  • D) 15+24
C: C=2R·sin(\(\dfrac{Δ}{2}\)) → R=947.77' L: L=\(\dfrac{2πRΔ}{360}\)=578.96' Station U: station U = 12+45+578.96 = 18+23.96 ≈ 18+24. Program S's input cycle includes C (chord) as a prompt — enter C=570, Q?=35° (Δ, as DMS), leave R?=0 to solve for it, then read L directly off the A output.

Answer: C
Q42. Backsight and foresight distances should be equal so that
IIlevel
  • A) Negate random user errors
  • B) Negate rod rounding errors
  • C) Minimize refraction and earth curvature errors
  • D) Keep the math easy
Balancing BS/FS distances cancels the effects of refraction and earth curvature, which act equally (in the same direction) on both sights when distances match.

Answer: C
Q43. A declining curve on a mass diagram indicates
Varea
  • A) excavation
  • B) lower elevation
  • C) cut
  • D) embankment
A falling mass diagram curve indicates material is being used as fill (embankment) — not necessarily a lower ground elevation, since the diagram tracks cumulative earthwork volume, not terrain elevation.

Answer: D
Q44. In a closed traverse, departures failed to close by −0.79' and latitudes by +0.49'. Horizontal traverse distance is 5649.2'. What is the approximate accuracy of the measurement?
IIItravProgram A — partial
  • A) 1/18850
  • B) 1/7150
  • C) 1/6100
  • D) 1/11550
Error of closure: Error of closure = √(0.79²+0.49²) = 0.93 ft 5649.2/0.93: \(\dfrac{5649.2}{0.93}\) = 6074 → accuracy ≈ \(\dfrac{1}{6100}\). Same as the FS-exam ratio-of-error questions — Program A's misclosure output gives this distance directly if the traverse is entered as a full set of sides.

Answer: C
Q45. Starting at sta 7+47 the roadway will be repaved to a 2.1% slope. Existing centerline elevations are given via level notes (HI=465.80, FS 7.31 at 7+47, FS 8.14 at 8+23). What is the cut/fill at centerline 8+23?
Vvc
  • A) 0.77 fill
  • B) 0.77 cut
  • C) 2.43 fill
  • D) 2.43 cut
Elev existing 7+47: Elev existing 7+47 = 465.80−7.31=458.49 Proposed elev at 8+23: proposed elev at 8+23 = 458.49+(823−747)(0.021)=460.09 Existing elev at 8+23: existing elev at 8+23 = 465.80−8.14=457.66 Difference: difference = 460.09−457.66 = 2.43 fill.

Answer: C
Q46. A contour map is requested for a 0.8×1.8 mile rectangular area, drawn on 24"×36" plans (margins ignored). Which scale is appropriate?
IVphoto
  • A) 1"=300'
  • B) 1"=250'
  • C) 1"=200'
  • D) 1"=650'
0.8 mi/24 in: \(\dfrac{0.8 mi}{24 in}\)=\(\dfrac{176 ft}{in}\) 1.8 mi/36 in: \(\dfrac{1.8 mi}{36 in}\)=\(\dfrac{264 ft}{in}\) pick the larger (more conservative) requirement so both directions fit → 1"=300'.

Answer: A
Q47. A development company owns a square 1.5-acre lot; the outer 5 ft is sidewalk/parkway. The rest is a multiuse building with underground parking, requiring excavation 15 ft deep with a 2:1 cut slope on each side. What is the total volume of cut?
Varea
  • A) 32,000 CY
  • B) 26,000 CY
  • C) 29,400 CY
  • D) 28,450 CY
Lot side: Lot side = √(1.5×43,560) = 255.62' Building footprint side (inside the 5-ft parkway strip): building footprint side (inside the 5-ft parkway strip) = 245.62'. The 2:1 side-slope excavation forms a truncated-pyramid (frustum) shape below grade rather than a simple prism — solved via the frustum volume method (top area, bottom area, and the slope-widened dimensions at depth 15 ft), giving 26,000 CY. A common wrong answer (32,000 CY, the top-flagged selection here) comes from assuming the excavation walls are vertical instead of sloped.

Answer: B

C: C=2R·sin(\(\dfrac{Δ}{2}\)) → R =\(\dfrac{327}{(2·sin(51.9917^{\circ}))}\)= 207.51 ft. Enter C=327 (chord input), Q?=103.59 (Δ, DMS), leave R?=0 — Program S solves directly.

Answer: D
Q49. A slope stake note at RPSS Point D (sta 17+57, offset 15.60) reads: cut 1.17 to CP (catch point) 6.00 ft out; cut 1.7 to Toe at 5.1 ft (3:1 slope, CP-to-Toe); fill 0.9 to CL at 4.5 ft (5:1 slope, Toe-to-CL); ground/reference elevation 2136.03. Point E is at sta 1+35 with elevation 2115.32. What is the uniform grade between the centerline of D and the centerline of E?
Vvc

  • A) 1.00%
  • B) 1.30%
  • C) 1.20%
  • D) 1.40%
Rule: a number with no C or F label next to it is treated as a plus value (i.e., F). Elevation at D_CL = 2136.03 + 1.17 − 1.7 + 0.9 = 2136.40 ft Grade between centerlines of D and E: grade between centerlines of D and E =\(\dfrac{(2136.40-2115.32)}{(1757-135) \times 100}\)= 1.3%.

Answer: B
Q50. Which of the following has the highest accuracy for a horizontal control network?
Igis
  • A) Local control
  • B) Terrestrial-based control
  • C) Secondary control
  • D) Global-regional geodynamics
Order (highest to lowest accuracy): Global-regional geodynamics (GNSS Order AA, international deformation studies) → Primary control (Order A) → Secondary control (Order B, densifies within primary) → Terrestrial-based control (traverse/triangulation to first/second order, or GNSS Order C) → Local control (third-order class I/II, local construction reference).

Answer: D
Q51. A roadway is converted to include a Class III bike lane; sign placed at edge of roadway at Point B. Horizontal curve radius to centerline 634' (minus 25' to arc ACD = 609'), Δ=70°, split 31°/39° at Point C. Vertical profile: PVI 57+23 elev 125.64, G1=3.5%, G2=−1.8%. F-F section: 50' wide, 2% cross-slope, B at edge. What is the elevation at Point B?
VvcProgram P — partial

  • A) 121.01 ft
  • B) 122.01 ft
  • C) 112.62 ft
  • D) 118.95 ft
Arc ACD length: Arc ACD length =\(\dfrac{2π(609)(70)}{360}\)= 744.03' = L of the vertical curve (horiz and vert curve lengths coincide here) Arc AC: Arc AC =\(\dfrac{2π(609)(39)}{360}\)= 414.53' ElevBVC: elevBVC = 125.64−3.5(\(\dfrac{7.4403}{2}\)) = 112.62 ElevC via R: elevC via R=\(\dfrac{(-1.8-3.5)}{7.4403}\)=−0.7123, elevC=\(\dfrac{(-0.7123)(4.1453^{2})}{2}\)+3.5(4.1453)+112.62 = 121.01 ElevB: elevB = 121.01+0.02(50) = 122.01 ft. Program P directly gets elevC once BVC/L/G1/G2/x are known — the horizontal-curve arc-length geometry feeding x, and the final cross-slope offset, are both manual.

Answer: B
Q52. A vertical curve: BVC elev 567.92, G1=+1.78%, G2=−4.10%, L=750', EVC at sta 16+32. What is the station and elevation of the high point of the curve?
VvcProgram P — full
  • A) sta 6+55, elev 565.90
  • B) sta 11+67, elev 570.23
  • C) sta 11+09, elev 569.94
  • D) sta 6+55, elev 569.94
Sta BVC: sta BVC = 16+32−7+50 = 8+82 High point distance from BVC, D₀: high point distance from BVC, D₀ =\(\dfrac{LG}{(G-G')}\)=\(\dfrac{7.5(1.78)}{(1.78-(-4.1))}\)= 2.27 sta → station 8+82+2+27 = 11+09 Elev: elev =\(\dfrac{Rx^{2}}{2}\)+G1x+elevBVC with R=\(\dfrac{(-4.1-1.78)}{7.5}\)=−0.784 → elev = 569.94 ft. This is exactly Program P's high/low-point find — enter VPI/grades/L, run the appropriate part, and both station and elevation come out directly.

Answer: C
Q53. In an engineering project, what is the correct sequence used in developing a project from beginning to end?
Iintro
  • A) As-built, Construction Staking, Control, Topography
  • B) Construction Staking, Topography, Control, As-built
  • C) Control, Topography, Construction Staking, As-built
  • D) Topography, Control, As-built, Construction Staking
Control survey establishes basepoints → topographic survey maps existing conditions → construction staking marks locations for the engineering work → as-built survey records final elevations once complete.

Answer: C
Q54. BM #755 on Hartford Street has BS=7.1 ft, elevation 109.2 ft. Cross-sectional leveling at sta 3+78 on Jameson Drive gives FS/offset pairs: 5.7/36, 6.4/25, 1.9/13, 3.1/0, 4.9/7, 5.3/10, 3.3/20 (right side). What is the elevation 17 ft right of centerline?
IIlevel
  • A) 112.4 ft
  • B) 109.3
  • C) 107.1
  • D) 112.9 ft
Interpolate FS linearly between the 10-ft and 20-ft right readings: rate = (5.3−3.3)/(10−20) = −0.2 FS/ft FS at 17 ft: FS at 17 ft = −0.2×(17−10)+5.3 = 3.9 Elevation: elevation = 109.2+7.1−3.9 = 112.4 ft.

Answer: A
Q55. The Terrace View Apartment building will be ten equally sized floors. The first three floors are built; the FS rod was located at the face of the building. Given BM1=122.50, BS=4.10, FS=8.75, H=61.20 ft, vertical angle 24° to the top of the third floor, what will the final elevation be at the top of the finished tenth floor?
IIstadia

  • A) 153.85 ft
  • B) 201.15 ft
  • C) 237.85 ft
  • D) 129.85 ft
Elev base: Elev base = BM1+BS−FS = 122.50+4.10−8.75 = 117.85 Height of 3rd floor top: height of 3rd floor top = FS+H·tan(24°) = 8.75+61.20·tan24° = 36.00 ft → each floor = 12 ft Height of 10th floor: height of 10th floor = 120 ft Elev(10th floor): elev(10th floor) = 117.85+120 = 237.85 ft.

Answer: C
